chunks: ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn and ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad ibn Qūlawayh (may Allah have mercy on them) narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-‘Aṭṭār and ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā ibn ‘Ubayd ibn Yaqṭīn al-Yaqṭīnī, from someone who narrated to him, from Abū Khālid Dhī al-Shāmah, who said: Abū Usāmah narrated to me, saying: I heard Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever wishes to be in the neighbourhood of his Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the neighbourhood of ‘Ali and Fāṭimah, let him not neglect the Ziyārah of al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ‘Abdillāh; a common title for Imām Ja‘far al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.جِوَار: Neighbourhood or proximity; a spiritual status of closeness to the Prophet and Imams.
key_terms.زِيَارَةَ: Visitation; specifically referring to the ritual visitation of the shrines of the Imams.
key_terms.نَبِيِّهِ: His Prophet; referring to Prophet Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family).

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of visiting Imam al-Husayn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh presents this hadith as a foundational proof for the spiritual efficacy of visiting Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), linking the physical act of ziyarah to the metaphysical status of 'neighborhood' (jirār) with the Ahl al-Bayt. This tradition underscores the Shia theological view that the shrine of the martyr serves as a tangible locus of divine grace, ensuring the visitor's inclusion in the intimate circle of the Prophet, Ali, and Fatimah. It elevates the ritual of visitation from mere commemoration to a means of securing eternal proximity to the divine representatives.
